copy.blurb:
The model fancies Ecuador more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Germany. +8.8pp is a substantive gap; that's what fires this as a Pick on the home side.

Public Elo rates Germany 110 points higher than the other side (Ecuador 1790, Germany 1900). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Ecuador to win at 27%, the draw at 23%, and Germany to win at 50%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Ecuador on the win side reads 27%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Ecuador to win at 17%, the draw at 24%, and Germany to win at 57%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Ecuador side — 17% on the market, 27% on the engine, a +8.8pp gap.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Ecuador the lower bound is 21%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +3.9pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The point is selection, not a blanket call. Most matches the model and the market agree on. This is one of the ones where they don't, and the gap is on the Ecuador side specifically.

This number will move. The confirmed starting eleven, fitness news, weather at the venue, and any tournament suspension carried in from previous matches all feed back into the prior. With kickoff 24 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A wide Pick can collapse into a Pass if news moves enough of the read. Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades and does not recommend a wager.
